mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases both discount rates and input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of episodes where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which elevates wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month average, combined with a simultaneous decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1 growth), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month average and GDPC1 growth turns negative.
